data.description:
## Story

As an epic author working in the DSO planning system, I can add a dedicated `## Closure Checks` section to epic and story ticket bodies so that durable end-state acceptance criteria are cleanly separated from one-time transitional closure work — preventing completion-verifier from treating transitional steps as persistent success criteria.

## Done Definitions

- DD1: `## Closure Checks` section template added to epic and story ticket body templates; section placement is **after** `## Success Criteria` to preserve sequential parser compatibility with ticket-migrate-brainstorm-tags.sh and similar scanners
- DD2: `plugins/dso/skills/shared/prompts/verifiable-sc-check.md` updated with option **(c) Route to Closure Checks** — criteria that represent durable end-state intent but fail the session-infeasibility check can be routed to `## Closure Checks` instead of being forced into bad proxies (option a) or deferred as DEFERRED_MEASUREMENT (option b)
- DD3: Schema migration sentinel `v1.2.0` added to `ticket-migrate-brainstorm-tags.sh` or a new `ticket-migrate-closure-checks-v1.sh` script; backward-compat: tickets lacking `## Closure Checks` are treated as having an empty section (pass, not fail)

← Satisfies: "SC1: ## Closure Checks section template established in epic and story ticket body templates"
← Satisfies: "SC2: verifiable-sc-check.md litmus rule updated to include option (c) Route to Closure Checks"

## Considerations

- **Section ordering (critical)**: `## Closure Checks` MUST appear after `## Success Criteria` in all templates. Scripts that scan ticket bodies sequentially (ticket-migrate-brainstorm-tags.sh, tag-extraction parsers) will misread content if a new `##` section appears before `## Success Criteria`. Validate placement in templates before committing.
- **Backward-compat sentinel**: v1.2.0 schema sentinel must be idempotent — running the migration script twice on the same ticket produces the same result; already-migrated tickets are skipped.

## Escalation Policy

Escalate when blocked — agents proceed unless a significant assumption is required that could send implementation in the wrong direction. All assumptions made without escalating are documented.
data.title: As an epic author, I can define Closure Checks in a dedicated ## Closure Checks section so end-state intent is cleanly separated from transitional work
